challenges.claim: The rationale calls Ps.119.105 the stanza's best-known line — an unquantified reception-history superlative that no staged artifact can decide, the same class the campaign already ruled on for bare rarity claims.
challenges.evidence: The claim is about reception outside the text. sweep.py is book-internal — it offers a WEB phrase mode over 2461 WEB verses and byte / accent-stripped / skeleton modes over 2527 MT verses — and psalm_device_inventory.json carries no reception data, so no digit-bearing sweep in this toolkit can support or refute it. It also escapes the automated gate by construction: check_universals.py dampens superlatives whose token is on its EST_ALLOW list, which contains the string 'best-', so 'best-known' passes unflagged; running check_universals.py over this cluster's 8 rows returns claims_seen 22, flag_count 1, and this claim is not the 1 flagged item. The book strategy's errata register already fixes the remedy for the same class — an unquantified rarity claim that propagated into row prose must be dropped or scoped explicitly, never asserted bare — and the same remedy applies here. The seam is untouched: 8 of 8 verses Ps.119.105-Ps.119.112 open on U+05E0 and Ps.119.113 opens on U+05E1 (consonantal_index.json), and נֵר (oshb:Ps.119.105, byte tier) is token 1 of its verse.
